statement: Two circles, with radii 9 cm and 4 cm, touch each other. Both circles also touch the same straight line and lie on the same side of it. How far apart are the two points where the circles touch the line?

choices.misconception: I took the square root of 9 x 4 = 36 and forgot to double it.
I took the distance between the centres, 13, and subtracted the difference in heights, 5, instead of using Pythagoras.
I gave the distance between the centres, 9 + 4, instead of the distance along the line.

hints: Draw it: join the centres, and drop radii to the line.

The radii to the line are perpendicular to it, and the segment joining the centres passes through the point where the circles touch. Cut off a right-angled triangle from this shape and use Pythagoras.
The centres are 9 + 4 = 13 apart, and their heights above the line differ by 9 - 4 = 5.

solutions.reliable: The radii to the touching points are perpendicular to the line. The segment joining the centres passes through the point where the circles touch, so it has length 9 + 4 = 13. Draw a line parallel to the given line from the smaller centre to the larger radius: it makes a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 13 and vertical side 9 - 4 = 5. Its horizontal side equals the distance between the touching points, which is the square root of 169 - 25 = 144, so 12 cm. The transferable idea: for touching circles, join the centres and drop radii to the tangent line to make a right-angled triangle.
solutions.elegant: As soon as the diagram is drawn, a 5, 12, 13 triangle appears: 13 between the centres and 5 difference in height leave 12 along the line.

whyOnTest: Touching circles: the distance between the centres is the sum of the radii, and radii meet tangent lines at right angles, which builds a Pythagoras triangle.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
